title: The Daughter Who Wanted to Navigate

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE IX: REPAIR, FAIRNESS AND MANY FUTURES (LCI-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume V concepts (401-500), the 30 themes and the five deeper subjects: old wrongs and their repair, who is heard, prejudice and fairness, care for minds and bodies, animals and hard tradeoffs, inventions and bad inventions, family life, and an island that keeps choosing its own future.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A young woman wants to navigate but her family expects pottery: support her choice, or ask her to do both.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject)'s family has made pots for six generations, and everyone expects her to carry it on. She wants to learn to navigate by the stars. (friend), her parent, is hurt: who will make the pots? What should (friend) do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (friend) swallows hard and tells her to go. She learns from the navigators, and on her first voyage, she brings the canoe home through a storm by the stars. (friend) is on the beach, proud and afraid. The pots are made by a cousin.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) asks her to keep making pots too. She tries both, for a year, and is exhausted. Then she makes a choice, and it is navigation. (friend) understands it better now.
